questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Bologna because I wanted to go to Italy and experience the culture and thought that doing so in a "smaller" city would be better.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy, the University of Bologna is not super helpful, but they have the necessary information written online.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much, I used the university's website

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The housing situation in Bologna is quite difficult. I found it very similar to Copenhagen, both in price and availability.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In Bologna, it's a must to stay within the city walls. I would also suggest staying in the Eastern or southern part of the city center, as this part is less modern and more charming.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I arrived early and hence had no problem checking in, which is done through an online platform were you videochat with a coordinator. I know others had some trouble, because of limited capacity each day, and therefore had to try multiple times before succeeding.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Required information was available on the website and through mails sent to me.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted, no problems at all.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Either arrive early, or don't stress. I don't think it matters when you do, you will still get checked in from your day of arrival, but I'm not entirely sure.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In general, I found the courses to be easier than in Copenhagen. The exams I did were focused on the slides presented and were more tuned toward remembering the material.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar. Lectures are often three hours though.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Asset Management and Transition Risk
Climate Macroeconomics and Finance
Introduction to Financial Derivatives and Hedging
Machine Learning for Economists
Market Microstructure and Algorithmic Trading

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I found "Asset Management and Transition Risk", "Climate Macroeconomics and Finance" and "Introduction to Financial Derivatives and Hedging" to be fairly straightforward. The lectures are not particularly good, but I found this to be a general thing.

As for "Machine Learning for Economists" and "Market Microstructure and Algorithmic Trading" both require some work to pass and when I did them I needed to hand in a group project in the end, which is nice since you get to work with either local students or other exchange students but also requires to put up some work.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not any. I used more money on eating out than I initially thought I would.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Travelling in Italy, especially accommodation was more expensive than I thought it would be.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't use any of the non-academic opportunities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not sure of all, but at least some sports clubs were available.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Can't recommend any, since I haven't tried them.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel around in Italy. High-speed trains are really good in Italy and can be cheap if you order in well enough in advance. Also, Flixbus is very cheap and fairly reliable. Other than that Bologna is a really nice city to spend time in. Be sure to check out the hills south of the city for hikes in green surroundings and nice views.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I did courses with group work, through which I met some local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not any really. Though Italians do have almost "religious" traditions about their food, but they immediately know you're not Italian, and most of the time just joke about it.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Definitely the food and the more laid-back attitude towards life. Also, the whole culture around going out and being outside in cafees with friends is really cool, even in the winter.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make sure you bring enough money to go out and enjoy the city's restaurants and cafes, as well as traveling.

Don't do courses that take up too much of your time. Focus on enjoying life. 

Find your accommodation well in advance. I found accommodation to be more important than I thought I would.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No, not other than what is already mentioned.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and the experience of living in another country with a different culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Didn't have any major challenges. Perhaps prioritizing what to spend my money on :p

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
